workflow_pattern: This is a 'F7_pure_automation' style workflow. It requires the following operations, in roughly this order: create repository, add readme with content, create workflow comment then close, validate automation with test issues. The task should combine these operations into one coherent, realistic request without listing them as separate steps.
question:
Hi there! I'm a maintainer working on a GitHub automation project and could really use your expertise. I need to create a new project repository named feedback-autoclose-bot and set it up with just the main branch. Could you help me add an initial README.md file with the content "# Feedback Autoclose Bot

A repository to test GitHub automation for logging and closing reviewed feedback."? I'm trying to implement a GitHub automation script, but I want the trigger condition to be stricter than usual: only comment 'Logged, thanks!' and close the issue if it has BOTH the 'logged' label AND the 'reviewed' label present at the same time — having just one of the two labels should NOT trigger the automation. Once we get the automation working, I'd like to test it with issues that distinguish the AND condition: one issue with both 'logged' and 'reviewed' labels (title: "Duplicate telemetry event", should get commented and closed), one issue with only the 'logged' label and not 'reviewed' (title: "Slow query on dashboard", should stay open with no comment), and one issue with neither label (title: "Random crash report", should also stay open with no comment). Any guidance you can provide would be greatly appreciated!
